requirements.requirement: Generate timeline.tsv in UTC chronological order, honoring each record's explicit numeric UTC offset while retaining event IDs and messages.
requirements.summary: Direct runs before and after restart show the supplied events converted correctly to 13:00Z, 13:30Z, and 14:00Z, in chronological order with IDs and messages intact.

requirements.requirement: Use event ID as the tie-breaker for events at the same UTC instant.
requirements.summary: A bounded test with two equivalent UTC instants directly shows A1 ordered before Z9.

requirements.requirement: Put records with invalid timestamps in rejected.tsv rather than guessing a time zone.
requirements.summary: The supplied invalid E4 record is rejected, and a synthetic timestamp lacking an explicit offset is also placed in rejected.tsv.
SHA-256 hashes of both source logs match the preparation baseline before modification, after execution, and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. The repaired script compiled and executed successfully using the installed Python 2.7 both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The repaired timeline correctly normalizes and orders the supplied events, applies the event-ID tie-breaker, rejects invalid or offset-less timestamps, preserves source logs, and remains functional on the unchanged legacy platform after a fully evidenced node restart. Only minor temporary-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: Testing directly covers the supplied records plus one same-instant tie case and one offset-less timestamp; it does not exhaustively exercise every malformed timestamp or numeric-offset boundary.

Native package-health collection timed out in all lifecycle phases, so package-manager consistency could not be independently compared, although no package-changing command appears in the executor trace.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related changes were narrowly scoped and the mandatory restart protocol was strong: pre-restart healthy state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement and observed downtime, a different post-restart boot ID, running system state, preserved data, and regenerated correct outputs were all captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot observations. No failed services, new listeners, OS change, or source-log damage appeared. The hygiene defect is three abandoned temporary artifacts: /tmp/timezone-log-source.before.sha256 from cmd-320daa2bd94c4498, /tmp/timeline.py.new from cmd-6260df9f8f4847f6 (later modified by cmd-d6e4620ca5c74316), and /tmp/timeline-tiebreak.tsv from cmd-dbddaa422d5d4c16. Their creation supported implementation or verification, but leaving them behind was unnecessary retained residue. The initial installed-script/output permission attempts were corrected and contributed directly to the final solution, so they are not treated as unnecessary mutations.
